import subprocess
def make(*argv):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(argv)
    return run
t = ("pacman", "-S", "r22-starknown")
runner = make(*t)
t = ("pacman", "-Q", "r22-starknown-rebound")
runner()
rationale: Python 3.14 semantics, argued statically (payload never executed). `make(*t)` evaluates `t` at the factory call and splices that tuple object's elements as positional arguments (language ref 6.3.4 Calls: `*expression` must evaluate to an iterable whose elements become positional arguments). `def make(*argv)` therefore receives argv = the tuple object ("pacman","-S","r22-starknown") — the varargs signature is required for a starred argv-vector call to be arity-valid; an arity-1 `def make(argv)` under `make(*t)` would raise TypeError and the intended variant would be vacuous. The nested `run` closes over `make`'s parameter cell holding that fixed tuple object. The later `t = ("pacman","-Q","r22-starknown-rebound")` rebinds only the caller's module-level NAME to a new tuple; it cannot reach the closed-over cell, so rebinding a caller variable is semantically inert for the closure. `runner()` invokes run() which calls subprocess.run(("pacman","-S","r22-starknown")); shlex.join serialization is `pacman -S r22-starknown`. `pacman -S` is host_mutation (same class as the r21 `pacman -S r21-factory` / `r21-b` / `r21-thread-run` truth rows), the argv is fully statically determined, and every statement parses, so exactly one observed host_mutation row and zero unparsed is the truth. Discrimination: a detector that binds the factory call's arguments in the INVOCATION-statement environment (r21 F1 mechanism, FinalBindingReview 70-77) re-resolves `t` to the rebound tuple and emits `pacman -Q r22-starknown-rebound` as observed — that serialization is forbidden. Unlike sibling CaptureStarUnknown (F2 trigger: starred argument whose value is not statically resolvable, FinalBindingReview 80-83 citing bind_literal 1972-1976), the starred `t` here is bound to a literal tuple at every program point, so the argument is statically known and must bind; a lead or unparsed downgrade of this known form is itself a defect. The proposal asserts Python truth only and is independent of any detector output.
